### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you an environmental scientist who is passionate about protecting California from harmful and toxic substances? Are you looking to work in a dynamic and fast paced setting? Do you enjoy challenges and opportunities that require you to push your skills and abilities to new levels? Then consider joining the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit’s team!  

**As an Environmental Scientist you will have the opportunity to:**
* Work in conjunction with Senior Environmental Scientists (Specialist) of the Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit on the interpretation and application of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions available to different waste types and waste management practices including, but not limited to, recyclable materials;
* Develop responses to the inquiries from stakeholders for interpretation of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions;
* Review past DTSC decisions, correspondence, statutes, legislative analyses, regulations, rulemaking document (statement of reasons and federal registers), and any other information relevant to hazardous waste management practices for consistency in the application of regulatory and statutory interpretations;
* Develop and conduct research regarding the evaluation of hazardous waste criteria, including exclusions and exemptions, as a team member of the SB 158 Hazardous Waste Management Report and Plan project; and
* Participate in onsite visits to hazardous waste generation and treatment facilities to evaluate hazardous waste management activities in support of interpretive tasks.

**Desirable Qualifications We Look For:**
* Strong experience in written communication (memos, white papers, publications, fact sheets, FAQs, formal letters, etc.);
* Excellent oral and written skills;
* Experience researching and analyzing complex scientific and regulatory information and developing recommendations;
* Able to solve problems creatively and effectively;
* Knowledge of developing science\-based regulations and environmental policies or analyzing proposed legislation;
* An understanding of environmental regulation and/or hazardous waste management; and
* Experience in oral communication (outreach events/activities, customer interface, stakeholder meetings, presentations, etc.).

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


**Effective July 1, 2025, specific Bargaining Units and associated Excluded State employees are subject to a salary reduction between 2% \- 4\.62% in exchange for hours in the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025\) per month. For more details, please click here** https://hrmanual.calhr.ca.gov/Home/ManualItem/1/2113

The Department of Toxic Substances Control does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.**

jobs.description:
**We’re delighted you’re considering joining us!**


At Hill Physicians Medical Group, we’re shaping the healthcare of the future: actively managed care that prevents disease, supports those with chronic conditions and anticipates the needs of our members.

**Join Our Team!**


Hill Physicians has much to offer prospective employees. We’re regularly recognized as one of the “Best Places to Work in the Bay Area” and have been recognized as one of the “Healthiest Places to Work in the Bay Area.” When you join our team, you’re making a great choice for your professional career and your personal satisfaction.

**DE\&I Statement:**


At PriMed, your uniqueness is valued, celebrated, encouraged, supported, and embraced. Whatever your relationship with Hill Physicians, we welcome ALL that you are.


We value and respect your race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, religion, disabilities, experiences, perspectives, and other attributes. Our celebration of diversity and foundation of inclusion allows us to leverage our differences and capitalize on our similarities to better serve our communities. We do it because it's right!

**Job Description:**

**Overview**


The Data Analyst **Part Time** supports data\-informed initiatives, including clinical quality, financial performance, and population health by gathering, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data as a compelling story to the Hill Physicians team and its collaborating partners. Within this classification, analysts may focus on reporting and visualization, or analytical consultation and modeling. Data Analysts work as members of teams committed to using and promoting industry\-standard best practices and to addressing new problems with innovative solutions.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Transform data into actionable insights with narrative to drive strategic and operational decisions
* Conduct driver analysis to identify key factors influencing health outcomes and predict future utilization of health care services
* Provide consultation to internal stakeholders in understanding and responding to HPMG performance as measured by external bodies, e.g., health plans and the Integrated Healthcare Association, as well as variations in internal clinical and financial metrics
* Assist internal and external stakeholders with appropriate use of standardized reports, analytical approaches to population management and quality improvement programs, and program effectiveness evaluation
* Serve as analytical liaison with internal stakeholders, ensuring clear communication of data requirements and fostering collaboration to drive data\-driven decision\-making
* Use business understanding to appropriately implement logic specifications
* Independently develop analytic plan to address business questions
* Prepare presentations for non\-technical audiences
* Provide guidance and support to junior analysts, helping them develop their skills and understanding of data analysis and familiarity with data sets
* Utilize advanced querying techniques for complex data manipulation and statistical analyses

**Data Governance \& Compliance**

* Proactively perform quality assurance on all deliverables including researching and reconciling data discrepancies occurring among various information systems and reports
* Maintain high data quality standards to ensure that reports and analyses are accurate, timely, and reliable, enabling confident decision\-making
* Improve the organization’s quality assurance procedures
* Collaborate with appropriate IT teams and business stewards to improve the quality of data and information flows at Hill Physicians
* Ensure compliance with data governance frameworks and healthcare industry standards, including HIPAA

**Knowledge, Experience \& Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, business, informatics, statistics, public health, or related field with coursework in quantitative analysis
* Master’s degree preferred
* Minimum 3 years of professional analytics\-related experience.
* Demonstrated ability to exercise good judgment, prioritize multiple projects and problem\-solve under tight deadlines and resource constraints
* Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills and presentation skills, including ability to present complex technical concepts in a clear, concise manner to audiences with varying levels of technical understanding
* Demonstrated ability to work independently and to function as an integral part of a team in a rapidly changing work environment, and to operate effectively with limited direction from management
* Intermediate understanding of healthcare\-specific datasets, including claims, clinical, and authorization data, with the ability to perform data extraction and analysis.
* Can independently solve moderately complex analytic problems and generate insights that inform decision\-making within specific business areas
* Understanding of data pipelines from source systems (e.g. EPIC) into data warehousing or other downstream data sources
* Experience with chronic disease identification, utilization trending, outlier analysis, quality metrics, and tracking of other health performance indicators.
* Proficiency in Microsoft suite, including pivot tables and advanced formulas and functions
* Proficiency in querying languages such as SQL
* Experience with advanced data visualization tools such as Tableau or GIS software (ArcGIS) preferred
* Experience with advanced analytic programs/languages such as SAS or R preferred

**Additional Information:**


Salary: $48,700\.00 \- $63,925\.00 Annual

**Hill Physicians is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting\-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

  

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self\-motivated, Entry\-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.


In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas\-to\-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.


This position is primarily remote, with limited, as\-needed travel or occasional site visits. **Only those in PST or MST will be considered.**Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.


This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD\&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT \- paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K\-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. **Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.** The deadline to apply is 09/3/2026\.

 **Your Role**:

* Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
* Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
* Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
* Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
* Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
* Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
* Coordinate with on\-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
* Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
* Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
* Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
* Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
* Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
* Valid driver’s license.
* Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
* Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.

‎


Performs advanced provider data management activities that support the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of provider and network information across enterprise systems. Processes provider data transactions, validates information, resolves non\-routine data discrepancies, and maintains provider records while following established operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and department standards. Partners with Contracting, Credentialing, Provider Relations, and other internal teams to support accurate provider data used for network operations, provider directories, claims processing, and regulatory reporting.  

The Network Data Management Specialist III works independently with limited supervision and is routinely relied upon to resolve non\-routine operational issues, support process improvement efforts, and provide guidance to peers. Decisions impact team output, data quality, and operational effectiveness within the provider data management function.
‎

**How will you make an impact \& Requirements**

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Process provider data transactions by entering, updating, validating, and maintaining provider and network information across multiple provider data management systems.
* Review provider demographic, contractual, credentialing, and network participation information for accuracy and completeness, resolving non\-routine discrepancies using established procedures.
* Perform provider data quality reviews and validation activities to support accurate provider directories, claims processing, regulatory reporting, and operational processes.
* Research provider data discrepancies and coordinate corrections with Contracting, Credentialing, Provider Relations, and other internal departments following established workflows.
* Maintain provider data documentation, processing records, and operational reference materials in accordance with departmental procedures and quality standards.
* Provide day\-to\-day guidance to team members on provider data entry procedures, system navigation, and established work processes while serving as a resource for routine operational questions.
* Identify operational issues and recommend improvements that increase provider data accuracy, processing efficiency, and consistency.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Associate's degree or bachelor's degree preferred; high school diploma or equivalent with relevant experience may also be considered
* 3\+ years of provider data management, managed care, healthcare operations, or related experience.
* Working knowledge of provider data management processes, provider directory maintenance, and healthcare network operations.
* Demonstrated experience performing provider data entry, validation, reconciliation, and maintenance within provider data management systems.
* Excellent attention to detail with the ability to accurately process large volumes of provider data while following established operational procedures and complex work processes.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with internal stakeholders.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and provider data management systems; experience with reporting tools or data validation applications preferred.

jobs.title: Travel Data Analyst (Transportation Planning Technician 3)
jobs.description:
**Description**
---------------


**About WSDOT**


The Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) is a multimodal agency with a global reputation for excellence. Our dedicated workforce plans, designs, builds, and operates an integrated transportation system that safely and efficiently moves people and goods throughout the state. In addition to maintaining over 20,000 lane miles of state highway and 4,100 bridges, WSDOT leads an award\-winning Active Transportation Plan, manages the world's longest floating bridge, and operates the largest ferry system in the nation!

 **The Opportunity**


WSDOT is currently seeking a transportation data professional to support the collection, analysis, and reporting of reliable traffic information used to inform transportation decisions across Washington. This position plays an important role in transforming traffic data into meaningful information that supports policy, planning, research, safety, and roadway design. By helping ensure transportation data is accurate, accessible, and useful, this role enables WSDOT and its partners to make informed decisions that strengthen the safety and reliability of the state’s transportation system. This position contributes to WSDOT’s commitment to providing safe, reliable, and cost\-effective transportation options while advancing the Transportation Data, GIS, and Modeling Office’s goal of making better decisions through better data.

 **What to Expect**


Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, you/the Travel Data Analyst will:

* Analyze traffic volume, speed, and classification data to identify inaccuracies, atypical values, and incomplete data and take appropriate corrective action.
* Process short\-duration traffic counts, including reviewing documentation, estimating daily volumes, merging data files, and validating traffic statistics.
* Provide guidance to field technicians to ensure data collection complies with coding protocols and processing requirements.
* Monitor permanent traffic recorder data, document accuracy issues, and coordinate with appropriate staff to resolve data problems.
* Provide backup support for traffic recorder polling, time checks, problem tracking, and year\-end data edits.
* Fulfill and document internal and external traffic data requests and direct customers to appropriate WSDOT resources.
* Maintain procedures and institutional knowledge through documentation, staff training, and cross\-training.
* Identify and support improvements to traffic data processing procedures and practices.

 **Qualifications**


To be considered for this opportunity, the following competencies are required:

* Experience using strong attention to detail, critical thinking, and analysis skills to effectively perform data processing and/or analysis on medium to large datasets with a high degree of spatial and temporal variability. This includes a focus on identifying data anomalies and determining their source, as well as effectively summarizing the data using descriptive statistics and visualizations.
* Experience assessing priorities, managing workloads, and achieving tasks within expectations of quality and timeliness.
* Skills and abilities to perform job functions with limited supervision, while maintaining a high level of productivity.
* Ability to receive input and communicate clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing. This includes written composition skills sufficient to update procedures manuals in a clear and comprehensive fashion.
* Skills and abilities to work effectively within a team to support data\-related goals. This includes experience demonstrating responsibility, adaptability, and interpersonal skills (empathy, conflict resolution, active listening, etc.).
* Ability to maintain high levels of concentration over long periods to minimize errors during repetitive tasks.
* Ability and desire to critically assess current processes and provide suggested improvements to achieve efficiencies or bring products in closer alignment with customer needs.
* Ability to work at a computer for hours at a time.
* General computer literacy, including proficiency with databases, the internet, and the Microsoft Office suite of software.
* Demonstrates a desire for learning and growth.
* Demonstrates a willingness to take action to meet the needs of others.

  

It is preferred that qualified candidates also demonstrate:

* Experience processing traffic count data, including accurately evaluating and summarizing such data using an advanced knowledge of temporal variation in traffic patterns, spatial variation in traffic patterns, and traffic counting equipment and methods.
* Experience coding data to the WSDOT linear referencing system and/or analyzing data coded to that system.
* Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel.

 **Important Notes**

* This position is eligible for remote work up to 100%, per supervisor’s approval and works a Monday through Friday schedule, five 8\-hour days, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional travel may be required, such as attending a conference, typically no more than once per year.

### **Job Summary**

INSTARR welcomes applications for a Temporary Field Technician!
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.
### **Who We Are**

As the University's oldest institute, INSTAAR has a long history of responding to pressing environmental issues including climate change. Our traditional focus has been on alpine, Arctic, and Antarctic regions, where effects of global change are especially pronounced. In recent decades, our research has broadened to include environmental challenges that span local, regional, and global scales. INSTAAR’s research activities integrate field studies, state\-of\-the\-art laboratory experiments, sample analysis, and numerical and laboratory modeling. Our field sites are located across all seven continents and the world's oceans.


Our expertise across disciplines helps us generate influential science that can inform public and policy decisions and move us toward a more sustainable society. INSTAAR's national and international research leadership is augmented by exceptional strength in graduate education and bringing undergraduates into the research process.


### **What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be**

* Assist in monthly fieldwork in alpine regions across the Front Range of Colorado.
* Assist in general lab analyses and tasks, including bottle and dish cleaning, water quality analyses, and other general lab work.
* Assist in data entry and metadata creation.


### **What You Should Know**

* Anticipated start date of September 4, 2026\.


### **What We Can Offer**

$22\.00 \- $23\.00/hour.


### **Benefits**

Temporary positions at the University of Colorado are not benefits\-eligible, however, all positions are eligible for paid sick leave.
### **Be Statements**

Be ambitious. Be groundbreaking. Be Boulder.
### **What We Require**

* Undergraduate degree.


### **What You Will Need**

* Experience with limnological field skills including sediment coring, van dorn sampling, and water travel.
* Experience in analytical laboratory skills, including experience with limnological field skills including sediment coring, van dorn sampling, and water travel.
* Experience in analytical laboratory skills including acid washing, and micro pipetting.

### **What We Would Like You to Have**

* Previous experience leading or assisting research projects with a focus on topics in biochemistry in aquatic environments. Experience working on diverse types of aquatic water bodies.


### **Special Instructions**

To apply, please submit the following materials:

* Resume or CV.


Please apply by 9/4/2026 for consideration.


Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, applications must be submitted through CU Boulder Jobs.


#### **Posting Contact Information**


**Posting Contact Name:** Boulder Campus Human Resources


**Posting Contact Email:** Recruiting@colorado.edu

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
**Data Analyst**
================


**Position Status:** Contingent upon contract award.
**Position Summary**
--------------------


Conduct reproducible public health data management, surveillance analysis, statistical analysis, visualization, and reporting that supports DNPAO scientific, programmatic, policy, and evaluation decisions. This role supports DNPAO epidemiology, surveillance, evaluation, policy analysis, and program\-impact reporting. Assignments may involve public\-use datasets such as NHANES, NHIS, BRFSS, YRBS, NIS, mPINC, or NSCH; large administrative and recipient datasets; GIS, mobility, image, or policy\-text data; R and Python analyses; dashboard and scorecard production; data\-quality checks; and reproducible documentation for scientific and decision\-making products.
**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------


* Acquire, clean, transform, merge, validate, and maintain public health and program datasets.
* Conduct descriptive, inferential, regression, trend, geospatial, policy, or other appropriate analyses.
* Use R, Python, SAS, SQL, visualization, or GIS tools as appropriate to the assignment.
* Develop tables, figures, maps, dashboards, scorecards, and accessible visualizations.
* Create reproducible code, data dictionaries, methods, benchmarks, and quality\-control documentation.
* Communicate findings, limitations, discrepancies, and recommendations to technical and program audiences.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------


* Education: Bachelor's degree.
* Experience: At least 5 years of experience analyzing public health, epidemiologic, surveillance, evaluation, administrative, policy, or large\-scale research data. Demonstrated proficiency with relevant tools such as R, Python, SAS, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or GIS and experience with data cleaning, quality assurance, reproducible code, visualization, interpretation, and technical documentation are strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to produce accurate, timely, and high\-quality work in a multidisciplinary, deadline\-driven environment.
* Strong written and verbal communication, collaboration, organization, judgment, and client\-service skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------


* Prior experience supporting CDC, HHS, another federal health agency, a public health recipient network, or a comparable mission\-focused organization.

**Core Competencies**
---------------------


Public service orientation; technical credibility; cultural responsiveness; collaboration; clear communication; accountability; adaptability; quality focus; sound judgment; and the ability to work effectively with CDC staff, recipients, partners, subcontractors, and subject matter experts.

*in accordance with applicable federal law.*

### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you an environmental scientist who is passionate about protecting California from harmful and toxic substances? Are you looking to work in a dynamic and fast paced setting? Do you enjoy challenges and opportunities that require you to push your skills and abilities to new levels? Then consider joining the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit’s team!  

**As an Environmental Scientist you will have the opportunity to:**
* Work in conjunction with Senior Environmental Scientists (Specialist) of the Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit on the interpretation and application of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions available to different waste types and waste management practices including, but not limited to, recyclable materials;
* Develop responses to the inquiries from stakeholders for interpretation of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions;
* Review past DTSC decisions, correspondence, statutes, legislative analyses, regulations, rulemaking document (statement of reasons and federal registers), and any other information relevant to hazardous waste management practices for consistency in the application of regulatory and statutory interpretations;
* Develop and conduct research regarding the evaluation of hazardous waste criteria, including exclusions and exemptions, as a team member of the SB 158 Hazardous Waste Management Report and Plan project; and
* Participate in onsite visits to hazardous waste generation and treatment facilities to evaluate hazardous waste management activities in support of interpretive tasks.

**Desirable Qualifications We Look For:**
* Strong experience in written communication (memos, white papers, publications, fact sheets, FAQs, formal letters, etc.);
* Excellent oral and written skills;
* Experience researching and analyzing complex scientific and regulatory information and developing recommendations;
* Able to solve problems creatively and effectively;
* Knowledge of developing science\-based regulations and environmental policies or analyzing proposed legislation;
* An understanding of environmental regulation and/or hazardous waste management; and
* Experience in oral communication (outreach events/activities, customer interface, stakeholder meetings, presentations, etc.).

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


**Effective July 1, 2025, specific Bargaining Units and associated Excluded State employees are subject to a salary reduction between 2% \- 4\.62% in exchange for hours in the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025\) per month. For more details, please click here** https://hrmanual.calhr.ca.gov/Home/ManualItem/1/2113  

  

  

**This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment. The Department of Toxic Substances Control does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.**  

  

**A hybrid schedule may be available for this position.**

new_jobs.title: Network Data Management Specialist III
new_jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**


‎


Performs advanced provider data management activities that support the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of provider and network information across enterprise systems. Processes provider data transactions, validates information, resolves non\-routine data discrepancies, and maintains provider records while following established operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and department standards. Partners with Contracting, Credentialing, Provider Relations, and other internal teams to support accurate provider data used for network operations, provider directories, claims processing, and regulatory reporting.  

The Network Data Management Specialist III works independently with limited supervision and is routinely relied upon to resolve non\-routine operational issues, support process improvement efforts, and provide guidance to peers. Decisions impact team output, data quality, and operational effectiveness within the provider data management function.
‎

**How will you make an impact \& Requirements**


‎

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Process provider data transactions by entering, updating, validating, and maintaining provider and network information across multiple provider data management systems.
* Review provider demographic, contractual, credentialing, and network participation information for accuracy and completeness, resolving non\-routine discrepancies using established procedures.
* Perform provider data quality reviews and validation activities to support accurate provider directories, claims processing, regulatory reporting, and operational processes.
* Research provider data discrepancies and coordinate corrections with Contracting, Credentialing, Provider Relations, and other internal departments following established workflows.
* Maintain provider data documentation, processing records, and operational reference materials in accordance with departmental procedures and quality standards.
* Provide day\-to\-day guidance to team members on provider data entry procedures, system navigation, and established work processes while serving as a resource for routine operational questions.
* Identify operational issues and recommend improvements that increase provider data accuracy, processing efficiency, and consistency.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Associate's degree or bachelor's degree preferred; high school diploma or equivalent with relevant experience may also be considered
* 3\+ years of provider data management, managed care, healthcare operations, or related experience.
* Working knowledge of provider data management processes, provider directory maintenance, and healthcare network operations.
* Demonstrated experience performing provider data entry, validation, reconciliation, and maintenance within provider data management systems.
* Excellent attention to detail with the ability to accurately process large volumes of provider data while following established operational procedures and complex work processes.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with internal stakeholders.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and provider data management systems; experience with reporting tools or data validation applications preferred.


‎

**Compensation Range:**


$26\.40
to

Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, internal equity, and business needs.*

-----------


These positions will serve as a Geologist, GS\-1350\-12/13 with the Department of the Interior, U.S. Geological Survey, Office of the Regional Director, Rocky Mountain Region, Central Energy Resources Science Center.


Learn more about this agency


  
**This job is open to**

### **Career transition (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL)**

### **Clarification from the agency**


This announcement is open to U.S. Citizen or National; and Career transition eligibles (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL).


  
**Duties**
----------


These positions are located within the Department of the Interior, U.S. Geological Survey, Office of the Regional Director, Rocky Mountain Region, Central Energy Resources Science Center, duty stationed in Lakewood, Colorado.  

  

At the full performance level **(GS\-13\)** the major duties of this position include, but are not limited to the following:  

  

1\. Compile, synthesize, interpret, and integrate diverse geologic datasets for a basin or region to construct geologic models for the generation, migration, accumulation, and/or production of geologic energy resources.  

2\. Conduct studies of geologic energy resources (e.g., petroleum, geothermal, uranium); these studies lead to assessments of undiscovered resources.  

3\. Collaborate with USGS colleagues to conduct quantitative assessments of geologic energy resources.  

4\. Participate in internal and external conferences and/or meetings as a technical representative. Participation in meetings and/or conferences is for the purpose of disseminating results.  

5\. Prepare reports documenting geologic energy assessment related work. These reports may be for internal USGS publications or for external journals and are intended to disseminate results.  

  

**Salary Range Information (Per Annum):** *\*First time hires to the federal government typically start at the beginning salary in the range for their respective grade level.*

This probationary period is an extension of the appointment process and therefore requires the agency to determine if continued employment would advance the public interest, meet the organization goals and mission of the agency, and/or otherwise promote the efficiency of the service. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, the agency will consider:
* your performance and conduct;
* the needs and interests of the agency;
* whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
* whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Under applicable law, the employment of an individual serving a probationary or trial period automatically terminates when that period ends unless the agency affirmatively certifies, in writing, that the individual's employment should continue and that their appointment should be finalized. In the absence of agency action to affirmatively certify continued employment beyond the probationary or trial period, such appointments are terminated.  

  

Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.
